steps.text: Peel mangos and remove the pits. Place the pits into a slow cooker, then roughly chop the mango and set aside. Place pork shoulder into the slow cooker and season with pepper, salt, and 1 teaspoon chipotle powder. Pour in balsamic vinegar and water.
Cover and cook on Low until the meat is very tender, 5 to 8 hours. Once done, drain the pork, discarding the cooking liquid and mango pits, and shred with two forks.

While pork is cooking, purée chopped mango in a blender until smooth, then pour into a saucepan along with honey, remaining chipotle powder, and whiskey. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer, stirring frequently, until mango has reduced and darkened slightly, about 10 minutes. Stir in barbecue sauce and remove from the heat.
Return shredded pork to the slow cooker and stir in mango barbecue sauce. Cover and cook on High until pork absorbs the barbecue sauce, 1 to 2 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Bourbon Mango Pulled Pork
raw_recipe.description: A recipe for pulled pork and mango BBQ sauce that balances spicy, smoky, and sweet. It's easy to prepare in the slow cooker and makes a great sandwich.

review.reviewBody: Made it for a party. Some of the comments I heard besides "delicious" were "This is definately a two plater" I did make my own version. After slow cooking 10 pounds for 14 hours, I

This is absolutely amazing. I had a 6lb butt roast, so it was too big for my slow cooker. Instead I put it in a dutch oven in the oven at 300 degrees for 5 hours. It was full flavored and fall apart when I took it out. I also used 3 mangoes rather than 2, and it was the right call. My BBQ sauce was Stubbs Smokey Mesquite, and once again, it was the correct choice. I only used 1 bottle though, as any more would have been too much, and overwhelmed the mango. 

My wife, who isn't a huge pork fan, went nuts when I let her taste it. This is my new go-to pulled pork recipe. Thank you!

I used a pork butt and pressure cooker for this recipe, which only took about one hour for the pork to cook and become very tender. I then let the pork simmer in the sauce for about 20 minutes. I only added about 9 ounces of Sweet Baby Ray's bbq sauce, and that was plenty. I also used regular chili powder instead of chipotle. My picky eating husband loved it. He even brought some to work for his co-worker, who really enjoyed it as well.

I just made this for the previous weekend. It was fantabulous! I used a larger pork shoulder, closer to 10 lbs, so I doubled the chili powder, black pepper and salt, also I used it as a rub and let it sit in the fridge for 8-10 hours before putting it in the slow cooker. I made this for my son and I. I like the spicy stuff, he does not, so I used a honey BBQ sauce to sweeten and somewhat mask the chipotle chili powder. It had just a hint of heat, enough to notice, but not enough to stop my son from eating it! When I make it for myself, I will probably spice it up more and cut back on the sauce a little bit.

Great starter recipe! However, I don't care for mangos, so I substituted peaches instead. I used four medium peaches, cut and pureed for the sauce, along with the bourbon. I didn't use nearly as much bbq sauce as the recipe called for. Definitely not needed, unless you like soupy pulled pork. I also created a rub of chili powder, garlic powder and crushed red pepper and put in on the pork to sit overnight in the fridge. In the morning, I put in the slow cooker with balsamic vinegar mixture, along with juice from canned peaches. The canned peaches were added to the fresh puree at the end. Delicious!

Tangy and sweet with a little bit of a zing. Loved it. I diced the mangos quite small then used a whisk to blend the honey and bourbon until it was soupy. Kept the mangos a bit "chunky" because I happen to love mangos. Substituted ground Cayenne Pepper and Chili powder instead of the Chipolte.

I have made this recipe for small groups of 10 to large groups of 100. Always a hit. Instead of using chipotle powder, I use canned chipotle peppers. Coarsely chop a small can to cook with the pork in balsamic vinegar and water. I also use several peppers when I puree the mango in the blender. I also add a cup of Woody's BBQ concentrate to get a smokey taste to the sauce. The canned chipotle peppers bring a nice hint of heat, which is countered with the mango and honey. I also start adding the bbq sauce in small quantities so it will not overpower the mango bourbon base.

This was absolutely delicious. Unfortunately I had to use regular chili powder as I failed to purchase the chipotle chili powder. It was still amazing. My roast was 6 pounds so I increased the other ingredients by I 1/2 times to compensate for the larger piece of meat as well as cooking longer. I did cook for the full 2 hours after adding the sauce to the shredded pork at the end. Yum yum. It is a keeper. Next time I will be sure to purchase the correct chili powder. I forgot to mention that I made the absolutely awesome barbecue sauce to use in this recipe also from this website, but following another reviewers suggestion used bourbon instead of rum.

This was absolutely flavorful!!! My kids loved it!!!! Tweaked it a little by using 2 cans of mangos and adding some brown sugar to step 1. I placed about 6 slices of the mangos from the can and poured the juices from the can of mangos into the slow cooker. Also made sure that the there was enough water covering the pork while it was in slow cooker.
Absolutely loved it and it was ono- good with laulau!!!

I used this recipe as inspiration for the pulled pork I made for a friend's wedding. It was a hit with the 150 guests! I used a rub of paprika, chili powder, thyme, salt and pepper on the pork in the fridge overnight before cooking it. I cooked it in the oven for about 8 hours at very low temp. We pulled the pork the night before the wedding and made the sauce and warmed everything through the morning of. It was worth all the prep work!
Grandkids are picky eaters (3 and 5), but they wolfed it down. Us adults really liked it too!

Love this recipe as is, it's perfect. I've experimented with the sauce using different fruits, bbq sauces and bourbons to give it a different flavor. I've used blackberries, blue berries, cherries and just made the sauce with peaches to use on sloppy joes. Absolutely love it!!!
Been making this for years. Love it the only thing I change is I add a little smoked paprika to the rub and a bit more Balsamic vinegar.

Easy and delicious! I used “Southern Comfort Cherry” ( don’t know where it came from but it added a nice flavor.) The pork took longer to cook but it was worth the wait. Also, no mangoes were available so I used fresh pineapple. It was a great New Year’s Eve dinner.
Excellent! I never was that crazy about pulled pork until I tried this recipe! It's is so good! I love the mango and bourbon taste in it! I'm making this for a party in a couple weeks!
This recipe is so good, everyone’s favourite. You can adjust the taste to suit your own & it will always turn out great. I use extra mangos, cause why not? A winner in our house.
Wow this is excellent! Very flavorful, so yummmmm! I did add an extra tsp of honey. I also had to make my own BBQ sauce because I don't eat sugar,

I think the recipe is okay. To me I would add less bar b que sauce because it overpowered the mango and definitely add the honey. I had crusty rolls and made a meal with this pulled pork recipe. I would definitely make this again but adjust the ingredients slightly.
